Thanks again for taking time today — appreciate the clear description of the regulatory constraints. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we have alignment before we loop infra/security in.

Top pain points & goals you stated
- Data residency: all PHI/PII must remain in Germany (Frankfurt) and be stored/processed within your VPC or on-prem environment.
- Air-gap option: for certain workloads (clinical analytics) you prefer a physically isolated on-prem cluster with no outbound internet egress.
- Audit & controls: strict audit trail requirements (immutable logs, 7+ years retention), SOC 2 and HITRUST alignment.
- Network constraints: customer-managed NAT, outbound through a narrow set of proxy IPs, mandatory mTLS for control-plane traffic.

What we can offer (high level)
- Private deployment: Redwood Private can run in your VPC (customer-owned subnet) with our control plane optionally in a customer-controlled environment.
- On-prem / air-gapped: we have an on-prem bundle used by other regulated customers — deploys as an appliance + orchestration layer, can be configured with zero outbound egress for model execution.
- Connectivity options: IP allowlist, static egress ranges for our optional control-plane connections, and a partner pattern where control-plane is replaced by customer-hosted services.

Immediate open items (we need answers from your network/security team)
1) Which option do you prefer for production workloads: (A) VPC with restricted egress and KMS in your cloud account, or (B) fully air-gapped on-prem?  Reply with preferred option.
2) If VPC, please confirm the subnet CIDR(s) and whether you require NAT for outbound (we can support NAT or public egress via proxy).
3) TLS/mTLS: do you have an internal CA we must accept, or should we provide certs and rotate them via your KMS?
4) Proxy / egress: list of proxy hostnames/IPs and whether outbound will be via an authenticated proxy.
5) Compliance evidence: can you share a short list of the compliance artifacts you need (SOC 2 type II report, penetration test report, data flow diagram) so we can package them.

Next steps (proposed)
- You: share answers to items 1-4 and attach any internal networking diagrams (by EOD Wed, Apr 22).
- Us: well produce a short VPC/on-prem networking checklist and an architecture diagram for your preferred option.
- Schedule: propose 30–45m follow-up with your network/security on Thu 23 Apr.

Attachments: Ive attached a draft networking checklist and a sample VPC diagram that covers the common controls we discussed.

Thanks — Ill loop Rishi (infra) once we have the preferred option.
